doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1965 European tour with Bill Evans and Herb Ellis story
summary: Konitz recalls Evans's drug trouble, the split trios, and a story about 'Detour Ahead'.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: At that point I thought he did. Then I realized that [it] was too difficult for him to move around even with his boys. Later on we did that European tour where Lennie played either with the Connie Kay duo, or solo, and I was playing with Bill Evans.
I don’t know the years too good.
When you and Bill played together that’s sixty-five.

Yeah. Bill, Niels Henning, and Alan Dawson. Bill was in bad shape and we ended up playing as two separate trios and just under the contract we played that last tune as a quartet. But that turned out great for me because I stretched out and enjoyed playing with those two guys a lot.
What was Bill’s problem? Was it drugs at the time?
So how was that affecting his playing?

It was affecting his attitude. Sitting around in the dressing room [I’d say] “What do you want to play?” [he’d say] “I don’t know what do you want to play?” He’d suggest a tune and I’d say okay and then when it came to the tune I couldn’t remember how it went and I’d say “you start.” That Herb Ellis tune “Detour Ahead”. Incidentally, I played in a club with Herb Ellis in Paris and we finished “Body and Soul” or whatever and I said “Do you know ‘Detour Ahead’?”
[Herb said] “Yeah I wrote that you mother fucker”.
I didn’t say that word, he did.
